category_title: Pupils with persistent disruptive and aggressive/abusive behavior
minimal_context: The student is expected to complete a silent reading assignment while seated among peers in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Everyone, please open your textbooks to page 42 and begin reading the chapter silently.

STUDENT: (Kicks the chair of the pupil sitting in front of them) I'm not reading this.

TUTOR: You need to stop distracting others and start your reading.

STUDENT: I wasn't even doing anything! He moved his chair back into my desk. It's his fault, not mine.

TUTOR: The whole class is waiting for you to be quiet. Stop arguing and get to work right now.

STUDENT: (Slams the textbook onto the floor and stands up) Why are you always picking on me in front of everyone?! I can’t control my behaviour when under pressure like this! I'm not doing your stupid work!

options.A: Maintain positive teacher-pupil relationships over time during classroom reading activities.
options.B: Represent information in various ways by including movement and physical activity for reading concepts.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each silent reading task.
options.D: Address the refinement of content and mechanics during the silent reading process.
